name: GitBook MCP
description: The GitBook MCP server gives AI agents a full read/write connection to your GitBook organization. Create and configure docs sites, spaces, and sections; draft, edit, and restructure content; open change requests and push updates for review; publish OpenAPI specs; and manage site customization — all through natural conversation, with OAuth sign-in or a personal access token. Pairs with the GitBook Skills plugin, which teaches agents how to use these capabilities effectively.

_published_faq.name: How do I add GitBook MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add GitBook MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.gitbook.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the GitBook MCP MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: GitBook MCP provides these MCP tools: create_change_request, describe_operation, get_page, get_site_structure, get_usage_guide, invoke_operation, list_sites, search, and submit_or_merge_change_request.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to GitBook MCP?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to GitBook MCP in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.

_published_faq.name: Does GitBook MCP MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: GitBook MCP requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
GitBook MCP is developed by GitBook. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
